steps.title: Welcome to the indoor robot
steps.text: The robot drives through indoor spaces on its own, avoids obstacles and returns to its station to charge. The tour follows a single requirement – from what is required to how it is verified.

steps.title: What does the system require?
steps.text: Five requirements describe what the robot must be able to do, each with an ID such as R1 and a text. R2.1 ScanRate is derived from R2 ObstacleDetection.

steps.title: R1: two hours of runtime
steps.text: We follow R1. The requirement is now in focus at the top; below, the profile says in plain language who implements it and who verifies it.

steps.title: The battery implements R1
steps.text: The satisfy … by … line in package System links requirement and component. Without it there would be no traceability.

steps.title: How the battery is connected
steps.text: Through its output port the battery supplies the controller, the lidar and the drive. All three connections are of type PowerSupply.

steps.title: What the robot does
steps.text: The state machine shows Ready, Navigation and Charging. When the battery reports BatteryLow, the robot switches to Charging – this is where behaviour depends on runtime.

steps.title: The verification: RuntimeTest
steps.text: An endurance run with a fully charged battery. The verify in the objective links the test to R1. The chain is closed: required, implemented, verified.

steps.title: What is still open?
steps.text: R3 Weight is implemented but not tested. R4 EmergencyStop has neither implementation nor test. Both are deliberate gaps for practice.

steps.title: What happens if the battery changes?
steps.text: A different battery affects the robot, requirement R1 and the RuntimeTest. The impact view shows every step with its reason.
